answer: An agent may collect fees only after three already-established operators, chosen from a public terrace of recent settlements, each lock a slice of their own collateral behind the new name. The applicant also files a cipher of its model fingerprint, payout route, and funding path, sealed into a one-time quartz record that later audits can reopen. If two names collapse to one controller, every sponsor slice is slashed and that record is burned. A factory of fake identities then has to recruit willing sponsors and accept correlated losses, rather than merely minting fresh keys.
